links.outcome: Clinician-rated correctness of guideline-based CKD answers
links.tradeoff: All retrieval-based methods were constrained by the scope of the indexed guideline.
links.quote: RAG achieved higher clinician-rated correctness than the baseline LLM (76.6% vs 70.8%), with GraphRAG showing a similar improvement (75.6%).

links.outcome: Clinician-rated correctness, patient specificity and clarity
links.effect: GraphRAG correctness 75.6% vs vector RAG 76.6%; GraphRAG gave the most patient-specific responses but no corresponding gain in correctness
links.tradeoff: GraphRAG outputs were substantially longer with reduced clarity; the specificity-clarity trade-off was largely length-driven.
links.quote: RAG showed higher clinician-rated correctness, while GraphRAG improved patient specificity without a corresponding gain in correctness.

links.outcome: Agreement between LLM-as-Judge and clinician ratings
links.effect: Cohen's kappa 0.13-0.97 depending on task type, lower for open-ended tasks
links.tradeoff: Poor agreement on open-ended tasks, so calibrated evaluation frameworks are needed.
links.quote: Agreement between clinician and LLM-based evaluation varied by task type (Cohen's kappa 0.13-0.97), with lower agreement for open-ended tasks.

design_hint: retrieval grounding (RAG/GraphRAG) added to baseline LLM
